findings.summary: ADR-011 faithfully records the authoritative DG-8 decision, is correctly numbered, and follows the established ADR format.
findings.detail: docs/decisions.md ADR-011 (Status Accepted, Date 2026-09-20) follows the Context/Decision/Consequences/Rejected alternatives/References structure used by ADR-001..ADR-010. It is appended after ADR-010 with 94 insertions and 0 deletions, so no existing ADR text was modified. It records exactly the user policy: no automatic duplicate/overlap detection or suppression, no Enhanced-internals dependency, overlap deferred to the user because Enhanced chooses its own overlay placement, output controlled only by existing poster and selector enable flags, and Spoiler Guard rendering normally with no special spoiler/hidden handling. The references (PLANS.md DG-8/task 5.10, architecture.md section 10, GOALS.md compatibility + success criterion 7, ADR-001/ADR-009) all exist and point to supported sources.

findings.summary: DG-8 is marked resolved consistently across the authoritative tracking documents, with no unresolved contradiction there.
findings.detail: PLANS.md (status line, task 5.10 checkbox, Task 5.10 status paragraph, Milestone 5 status row, Enhanced acceptance criterion, Phase 5 deliverable, DG-8 gate row, Enhanced risk row), docs/architecture.md (section 6 config list, section 10, section 13 testing, section 14 item 8), docs/implementation-readiness.md (Status, Basis, Former Action Disposition item 10, implementation-time question, new Resolved DG-8 section, Ready-for-Implementation checklist), docs/data-model.md (3.12 and 4.12 enhancedCoexistencePolicy rows plus prose), docs/changelog.md, and README.md all state the same resolved policy. The obsolete architecture statements ('ArrTags exposes a policy to disable or limit its server badges' and the standalone Spoiler Guard route-testing bullet) were replaced with the ADR-011 policy rather than left contradicting it.

findings.summary: The controlled-configuration claim is accurate and does not overstate what existing configuration can do.
findings.detail: MediaEligibility.IsBadgeSurface consults only PluginConfigurationSnapshot.BadgeMoviePosters/BadgeEpisodePosters (src/ArrTags/Media/MediaEligibility.cs:61-69), and renderer badge output is resolved through RendererConfiguration.Selectors / PluginConfigurationSnapshot.BadgeDefinitions before BadgeSelectorResolver.Resolve (src/ArrTags/Rendering/BadgeDefinitionResolver.cs:47). The docs accurately state these flags are the user's disable/limit control surface and do not claim automatic overlap detection, duplicate suppression, or a new knob. No production file changed (no src/ or .csproj edits), so no configuration schema or behavior was altered.

findings.summary: The coexistence tests are meaningful, host/runtime-free, and sensitive to the coupling they guard against.
findings.detail: The 7 tests in tests/ArrTags.Tests/EnhancedCoexistenceTests.cs use reflection over the real ArrTags assembly (typeof(Plugin).Assembly) to assert no referenced assembly name and no declared type name matches Enhanced/JellyfinEnhanced/Spoiler/Suppress/Blur/Hidden/Overlap, assert the listed policy-surface types expose no such member, and assert the renderer/publication/reconciliation/lifecycle enums expose no such value. The behavioral tests exercise real MediaEligibility, BadgeSelectorResolver, and SkiaBadgeRenderer with canonical inputs and vary only the poster flags and selector enablement. They run with 0 skips and no live host, live Enhanced install, or Skia native runtime (the renderer cases return pass-through before native decoding). A newly introduced Enhanced assembly reference, Enhanced/spoiler/suppression type, or enum branch would fail the corresponding assertion, so the checks are not trivially true.

findings.summary: The forbidden-token list includes the broad token 'blur', which is also a substring of 'bluray'; this is a latent false-positive risk, not a current defect.
findings.detail: ForbiddenNameTokens contains 'blur', which matches unrelated names such as 'Bluray'. No current production type or policy-surface member contains 'blur'/'bluray' (the only matches are XML doc comments in RadarrQuality.cs/SonarrQuality.cs), so all assertions pass today. A future legitimate member/type such as a Bluray source name would trip the tests. This is a minor maintainability note only and does not affect the correctness of task 5.10.

findings.summary: The Milestone 5 Enhanced acceptance criterion is checked while route/client validation remains task 5.11 and sibling criteria stay unchecked.
findings.detail: PLANS.md marks 'ArrTags does not interfere with Jellyfin Enhanced ...' as [x] while the other Milestone 5 acceptance criteria remain [ ] (all prior tasks also left them unchecked). Because ADR-011 frames coexistence as a policy/non-interference property and the docs explicitly state route/client confirmation remains task 5.11, this is not an overclaim of route coverage; it is noted only for tracking consistency.
